answer:
Use OpenFOAM.
Use the buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam solver.
Model a two-dimensional square cavity with side length L.
Use a 100 by 100 uniform mesh.
Assume laminar flow.
Use the Boussinesq approximation for buoyancy.
Set gravity to (0, -9.81, 0) m/s^2.
Set the working fluid properties to match air, with Prandtl number 0.71 and with cavity size and properties chosen to give Rayleigh number 10^4.
Set the Boussinesq reference temperature to 295 K.
Set the left wall temperature to fixedValue 300 K.
Set the right wall temperature to fixedValue 290 K.
Set the top wall temperature to zeroGradient.
Set the bottom wall temperature to zeroGradient.
Set the velocity on all walls to noSlip.
Set the pressure boundary conditions on all walls to fixedFluxPressure.
Set initial conditions to U=0, T=295 K, and p_rgh=0.
Run the transient simulation until the temperature and velocity fields reach a steady state.
Verify the final result against the de Vahl Davis benchmark for Ra=10^4 and Pr=0.71.
